items.q: A value 7.4 is given to 1 d.p. What are the lower and upper bounds?
hints: The bounds are half a unit of accuracy below and above the rounded value.
1 d.p. means the unit of accuracy is 0.1, so half of that is 0.05: 7.4 - 0.05 and 7.4 + 0.05.

items.q: A value 580 is given to 2 s.f. What are the lower and upper bounds?
hints: The bounds are half a unit of accuracy below and above the rounded value.
2 s.f. on 580 means the unit of accuracy is 10, so half of that is 5: 580 - 5 and 580 + 5.

items.q: A length 3.4 cm is correct to 1 d.p. State the error interval.
items.imageAlt: A number line showing the error interval 3.35 <= x < 3.45, closed circle at the lower bound, open circle at the upper bound.
items.imageCaption: 3.35 ≤ x < 3.45 — lower bound included, upper bound excluded.
hints: Write the lower and upper bounds as an inequality — the lower bound is included, the upper bound is not.
1 d.p. means half a unit either side: 3.4 - 0.05 and 3.4 + 0.05.

items.q: A mass 2.75 kg is given to 2 d.p. What is the upper bound?
hints: The upper bound is half a unit of accuracy above the rounded value.
2 d.p. means the unit of accuracy is 0.01, so half of that is 0.005: 2.75 + 0.005.

items.q: A population 4300 is given to 2 s.f. What is the lower bound?
hints: The lower bound is half a unit of accuracy below the rounded value.
2 s.f. on 4300 means the unit of accuracy is 100, so half of that is 50: 4300 - 50.

items.q: A number 9.81 is correct to 2 d.p. State the lower bound.
hints: The lower bound is half a unit of accuracy below the rounded value.
2 d.p. means the unit of accuracy is 0.01, so half of that is 0.005: 9.81 - 0.005.

items.q: A value 350 is given to the nearest 50. What are the lower and upper bounds?
hints: The bounds are half a unit of accuracy below and above the rounded value.
Nearest 50 means half a unit is 25: 350 - 25 and 350 + 25.

items.q: A length is 8.2 cm correct to 1 d.p. Find the lower bound.
hints: The lower bound is half a unit of accuracy below the rounded value.
1 d.p. means half a unit is 0.05: 8.2 - 0.05.

items.q: A width is 15 cm correct to the nearest cm. Find the upper bound.
hints: The upper bound is half a unit of accuracy above the rounded value.
Nearest cm means half a unit is 0.5: 15 + 0.5.

items.q: A time is 2.4 s correct to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound.
hints: The upper bound is half a unit of accuracy above the rounded value.
1 d.p. means half a unit is 0.05: 2.4 + 0.05.

items.q: A mass is 350 g correct to 2 s.f. Find the lower bound.
hints: The lower bound is half a unit of accuracy below the rounded value.
2 s.f. on 350 means the unit of accuracy is 10, so half of that is 5: 350 - 5.

items.q: A distance is 1.25 km correct to 2 d.p. Find the lower bound.
hints: The lower bound is half a unit of accuracy below the rounded value.
2 d.p. means half a unit is 0.005: 1.25 - 0.005.

items.q: A value is 74 correct to the nearest integer. Find the error interval.
hints: Write the lower and upper bounds as an inequality — the lower bound is included, the upper bound is not.
Nearest integer means half a unit either side: 74 - 0.5 and 74 + 0.5.

items.q: The error interval for a value is 6.5 <= x < 7.5. What is the rounded value?
hints: The rounded value sits exactly halfway between the two bounds.

items.q: A length is 5.2 cm and width is 3.1 cm, both correct to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound for the area.
hints: For a product, use the upper bound of each measurement to get the maximum possible area.
Upper bounds are 5.25 and 3.15, so area = 5.25 x 3.15.

items.q: A distance is 120 m and time is 15 s, both correct to the nearest integer. Find the upper bound for the speed.
hints: For a division, use the upper bound of the numerator and the lower bound of the denominator to maximise the result.
Upper bound of distance is 120.5, lower bound of time is 14.5, so speed = 120.5 / 14.5.

items.q: A rectangle is 8.4 m by 2.6 m, both to 1 d.p. Find the lower bound for the area.
hints: For a product, use the lower bound of each measurement to get the minimum possible area.
Lower bounds are 8.35 and 2.55, so area = 8.35 x 2.55.

items.q: A mass is 7.5 kg and 3 equal bags are made. Both values exact except the mass is correct to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound for one bag.
hints: For a division, use the upper bound of the numerator (the bag count is exact, so it doesn't change).
Upper bound of mass is 7.55, so one bag = 7.55 / 3.

items.q: A distance is 40 km correct to the nearest km and fuel used is 5 L correct to the nearest litre. Find the lower bound for km/L.
hints: For a division, use the lower bound of the numerator and the upper bound of the denominator to minimise the result.
Lower bound of distance is 39.5, upper bound of fuel is 5.5, so km/L = 39.5 / 5.5.

items.q: A square has side 6.0 cm correct to 1 d.p. Find the upper bound for its perimeter.
hints: For a sum of equal sides, use the upper bound of the side length, then multiply by 4.
Upper bound of the side is 6.05, so perimeter = 4 x 6.05.

items.q: A length is 20 cm and another is 12 cm, both correct to the nearest cm. Find the lower bound of the difference between them.
hints: For a subtraction, use the lower bound of the first value and the upper bound of the value being subtracted, to get the smallest possible difference.
Lower bound of 20 is 19.5; upper bound of 12 is 12.5, so 19.5 - 12.5.

items.q: A calculation gives 18.67391 for a length in cm. State an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: A raw calculator answer should usually be rounded to 3 significant figures for a real-world measurement.
18.67391 rounded to 3 s.f. is 18.7.

items.q: A population estimate is 2486.7 people. Give an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: People must be counted as whole numbers — round to the nearest integer.
2486.7 rounds to 2487.

items.q: A cost is 12.384 pounds. State an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: Money is usually given to the nearest penny — 2 decimal places.
12.384 rounded to 2 d.p. is 12.38.

items.q: A speed is 17.246 m/s. Give an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: A raw calculator answer should usually be rounded to 3 significant figures for a real-world measurement.
17.246 rounded to 3 s.f. is 17.2.

items.q: An area is 53.998 cm^2. State an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: A raw calculator answer should usually be rounded to 3 significant figures for a real-world measurement.
53.998 rounded to 3 s.f. is 54.0.

items.q: A journey time is 2.483 hours. State an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: A raw calculator answer should usually be rounded to 3 significant figures for a real-world measurement.
2.483 rounded to 3 s.f. is 2.48.

items.q: A stadium's crowd is estimated as 24875.6. State an appropriate degree of accuracy.
hints: A raw estimate should usually be rounded to 3 significant figures for a real-world count.
24875.6 rounded to 3 s.f. is 24900.
